chunks: A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ibn Mahboub, from Dawood al-Raqqi, who said:

I said to Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him): 'I am on a journey and the prayer time arrives, and there is no water with me, and it is said that water is nearby. Should I seek the water, searching right and left, while I am in the prayer time?' He (peace be upon him) said: 'Do not seek the water, but perform tayammum, for I fear that you will be left behind from your companions, become lost, and the predators will devour you.'
ai.seo_question: When is it better to perform tayammum instead of seeking water for prayer?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi illustrates the principle of 'priority of time' (tarjih al-waqt) in Shia jurisprudence, where the certainty of praying on time outweighs the possibility of finding water later. Imam al-Sadiq (AS) extends this ruling beyond mere delay to include the risk of danger (khawf al-darar), such as being devoured by beasts, thereby linking the validity of tayammum to the preservation of life and the timely fulfillment of the prayer obligation.

en.hubeali: A number of our companions, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad, from Ibn Mahboub, from Dawood Al Raqqy who said,

‘I said to Abu Abdullahasws, ‘I happen to be in the journey and the Salaat becomes due, and there is no water with me, and it is said that the water is nearby from us, should I seek the water left and right and I am in the time (for Salaat)?’ Heasws said: ‘Do not seek the water, but perform Tayammum, for Iasws fear upon you, being left behind from your companions, so would stray and the predators might devour you’.
en.sarwar: 6. A number of our people have narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from ibn Mahbub from Dawud al-Riqqiy who has said the following:

“I once said to abu ’Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam. ‘During a journey if I cannot find water when it is time of Salah (prayer); but it is said that water is nearby. Must I then search in the right and left directions when it is time for Salah (prayer)?’ He (the Imam) said, ‘Do not search for water, instead take Tayammum; I fear you may remain behind your companions and you may get lost or be eaten by the beasts.’”
